answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a refundable deposit that is slashed on proven fraud, so creating thousands of fake agents becomes expensive. Like a wharf charging every ship a berth fee before it can dock, the stake prices entry. Reputation then accrues slowly through verified work — a jade seal earned over time, not bought — while sable-flagged suspicious clusters face extra audits. An attacker must fund every fake identity and risk losing each stake, so mass fakery costs more than it can earn.
